metadataReview.note: Churchill's contemporary account of the action of 7 June 1896 places the Dervish camp in and beside the village of Firket, which stretched nearly a mile along the Nile below Firket mountain, and describes the Egyptian brigades clearing the village to the water's edge. The atlas point is the gazetteer node for the Ferka (Firket) village; the neighbouring peak carries the alternative name Jebel Firket. It is a village-sector reference, not the fortified ridge, the desert column's hills or the pursuit to Mograka and Suarda. The existing date is retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: Nominatim lookup of OpenStreetMap node 4307686547 (place=village, name:fr Ferka, name:en Ferka East, GNS populated place) returns latitude 20.9026620 and longitude 30.5786263, rounded to [30.5786,20.9027]. The adjacent GNS mountain node 4307686549 lists Jebel Firket and Jebel Ferka as alternative names, tying the Ferka spelling to Firket; the peak lies about 3 km north-east of the village, matching Churchill's description of the mountain on the left of the southward march with the village beyond. This is a village-sector reference, not a surveyed Dervish or Egyptian position, and no accuracy radius is claimed.
